name: Zones overlay
why: The real page with the four zones boxed and labelled: navigation, actions, links, preferences.

name: Wireframe map
why: A reading page as a wireframe with its levels of organization pulled out and tied to where they live: sections in the switcher, groups and pages in the sidebar, headings in the contents rail.

name: Exploded layers
why: The quiet details pulled out of the page and tied back to where they sit: the theme toggle in both places, the italic last-updated line, the split copy-page button, the star count and the language switcher.

name: Reading path
why: A numbered path over the muted page: orient, navigate, read, choose, act.

name: Four corners
why: One crop per zone, labelled by what you do there: navigate in the sidebar, act in the header, adjust or leave in the footer, read in the content column.

name: Redline pass
why: The old page with every deleted element struck in red and a legend beside it; the header rule is a line, and nothing touches.

name: Before / after split
why: Old and new at the same scale; deletions in red, the replacement row in blue.

name: The pile
why: The deleted pieces cut out of the old page, braced together into the single row that replaced them.

name: Peel the layers
why: Extra lines, links and buttons as translucent layers lifted off the new page, each called out in red; the page itself in blue.

name: Header strip
why: Where the old top band’s controls went: the search field became the ⌘K icon, the GitHub banner became the star pill, and the sidebar toggle went away because the sidebar now stays.

name: Navigation census
why: Every navigation or control surface numbered on both pages: the old page’s six in red, the new page’s three in blue.

name: Accordion anatomy
why: The new sidebar enlarged with a label for each part, and the two levels that live beyond it: the sections in the open switcher, tied to the switcher, and the headings in the contents rail, tied to the group heading.

name: Persistence strip
why: Three consecutive pages; the sidebar stays, only the active marker moves.

name: Sidebars side by side
why: The two sidebars at the same scale with bracketed labels.

name: One tree
why: The sidebar drawn as the tree it is, mapped onto the real crop.

name: Another section
why: The same accordion in two sections: the Quickstarts sidebar, and the React reference one click away in the switcher, same shape, same footer, same place.

name: Type specimen
why: Real type from the page at 110–220%, hung on one centre axis: the old docs’ single weight and grey first, then each new role, its sample right of nothing but the axis and its label set in the weight and style it names, with the spec beside it in mono.

name: Alignment
why: Top-aligned rows against the real centre-aligned switcher and footer rows.

name: Icons, not lists
why: The old paragraph-and-links against the About section’s three cards, each led by a solid icon.

name: Rules and space
why: The two 1px rules and the measured spacing at the top of the page.

name: Intro Quickstarts, before and after
why: The Introduction page’s Quickstarts section, old and new, at the same scale: eight centred logo tiles under a command line, versus eight cards with a solid icon, a name and one line each.

name: TOC slide (animated)
why: The Fumadocs table of contents on the Next.js quickstart, recorded live while scrolling: the active marker slides down the rail, an SVG path applied as a CSS mask. Delivered as GIF and MP4 as well as a still.

name: Solid vs outline
why: The old outline glyphs beside the solid glyphs the new docs use.

name: Corners
why: The old pill button and search field over the new button and copy control, at the same scale, beside the radius scale the new docs use with the pill struck out.

name: Flags, not emojis
why: The language menu with its custom matte flag SVGs beside the same list drawn with emoji flags, which are glossy and change from platform to platform.

name: Sidebar mask (animated)
why: The React reference sidebar recorded live: clicking from Configuration down through the Components children, the blue thumb sliding along the rail and through the bend where the tree nests. Delivered as MP4 and GIF as well as a still.

name: Localized
why: The same Introduction page in English and Chinese at the same scale. Dashed guides run across both: title, first sidebar item, header actions and the language row sit on the same lines, so spacing, alignment and order hold across languages.

name: Quiet scrollbar
why: The React reference sidebar with its scrollbar: a thin rounded thumb on a transparent track, enlarged beside it and measured; the same bar runs in code blocks and menus.

name: Hit list
why: The ten anti-patterns as a two-column list with solid x-marks.

name: Spot the anti-patterns
why: An illustrative generic mock with numbered red callouts; labelled as a mock.

name: Don’t / Do
why: Three real pairs cropped from old and new.

name: The fix for each
why: The hit list as a 3×3 card where every anti-pattern is struck out and its replacement written under it.

name: Poster
why: The hit list regrouped into clutter, navigation and language, every item marked with the set’s red x; the group names are the set’s ordinary labels.

name: Cover · exploded components
why: The page taken apart in a three-quarter perspective: the real content column, navigation, actions and contents rail, and the links and preferences rows each hover on their own glass pane above a ghost wireframe of the page, held at their true positions by dashed posts. Straight-on perspective, no text, blue background.

name: Cover · exploded components (OpenGraph 1200×630)
why: The exploded-components stack at OpenGraph size, straight on, on the blue-toned export.

name: OpenGraph · exploded components, light theme (1200×630)
why: The OpenGraph image with the docs in their light theme, on the same ground as the dark one.

name: Cover · exploded components, light theme
why: The cover with the docs in their light theme: the same dark blue ground and scale as the header cover, the page panes and the wireframe they hover over in paper and ink.

name: Cover · wireframe map
why: The wireframe-map direction with no text: the fleshed-out wireframe of the real page with the four zones in blue, and real crops of the live docs tied to their zones, on the blue-toned export.

name: Cover · wireframe map, light theme
why: The wireframe-map direction with the docs in their light theme: paper plate, ink bars, light crops, the same blue-toned export.

name: OpenGraph · wireframe map, cleaned (1200×630)
why: The OpenGraph image: the wireframe of the real page alone, no crops, no labels, no numbers, the four zones in blue, on the blue-toned export. Nothing but the diagram.

name: OpenGraph · wireframe map, light theme (1200×630)
why: The wireframe of the real page alone in its light theme, the four zones in blue, on the blue-toned export.
